evidence: "there are exactly n − 1 fiber conduits"; "data can travel between any two racks via exactly one sequence of conduits"; both surviving solutions build adjacency lists and perform DFS-based subtree marking
affordance_in_statement: A single, non-redundant network topology links them all: there are exactly n − 1 fiber conduits, and data can travel between any two racks via exactly one sequence of conduits.

removal_suggestion: To remove the reduction, re-present the network as allowing multiple possible routes and make connectivity depend on choosing among alternative routes, rather than stating that every pair has exactly one conduit sequence. Because m = n − 1 is immutable, this would need to be expressed through the scenario or edge semantics rather than by merely changing the numeric bound.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: The recursive graph traversal overflowed or otherwise failed at runtime on a worst-case deep tree, despite the underlying reduction being appropriate.
Its implementation produced a wrong answer, indicating that its traversal did not correctly accumulate exactly the edges in the minimal subtree connecting all leased racks.

recommended_edit: Replace the explicit unique-path/tree presentation with a scenario in which activating conduits requires selecting among alternative routes or satisfying an additional routing condition, while preserving the input and output formats. This is the only shared structural assumption used by both surviving solutions.
regression_risk: Changing only traversal wording will not affect the already-defeated models; changing the topology semantics could allow a more robust graph algorithm to solve the revised problem.
